title: Deep Agents — a middleware stack on LangChain's loop, on LangGraph's runtime

nodes.label: Your application
nodes.excerpt: The core package is a library. An application calls create_deep_agent with a model, optional tools, a backend, a checkpointer, and stack arguments — and gets back a compiled LangGraph graph to invoke or stream. Nothing runs until the application runs it.

nodes.label: Deep Agents Code — dcode
nodes.excerpt: The batteries-included product on the SDK: a terminal client and an agent-server process, TUI plus headless mode, layered config, its own tools, skills, hooks, and threat model. It wires the SDK with a CompositeBackend over LocalShellBackend — the product chooses host shell access and builds its approval flow on top.

nodes.label: deepagents-acp
nodes.excerpt: Serves a deep agent over the Agent Client Protocol — JSON-RPC over stdio, via the acp Python SDK — for editor integration.

nodes.label: Talon — long-running host
nodes.excerpt: An experimental host for agents that stay alive: channel adapters (WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack), a persistent cron scheduler, MCP tool loading from ~/.deepagents/.mcp.json, LangGraph checkpoints in a local SQLite file. Its README is frank that production-grade HITL and multi-tenant controls are not implemented; its per-invocation recursion limit defaults to 500.

nodes.label: Sandbox partner packages
nodes.excerpt: Concrete BaseSandbox implementations — remote sandboxes with real process isolation. Isolation exists in this ecosystem only here, as separate partner packages a caller chooses and wires in; the core package ships no sandbox implementation.

nodes.label: create_deep_agent() — assembly
nodes.excerpt: Roughly 700 lines of construction and no loop: resolves the model and its harness profile, defaults the backend to StateBackend(), builds the middleware stack, compiles subagents, composes the system prompt — then returns LangChain's create_agent(...) with recursion_limit 9_999 and ls_integration: deepagents metadata stamped on.

links.label: graph.py:989-1010 — the create_agent return + stamped config

nodes.label: The middleware stack
nodes.excerpt: The product. Filesystem, SubAgent, Deep Agents' own summarization, PatchToolCalls — then conditional skills, LangChain prompt caching, memory, LangChain HITL, unsupported-content. An ordered list of LangChain AgentMiddleware: replaceable by name, excludable by profile — except Filesystem and SubAgent, whose exclusion raises ValueError (protected scaffolding).

nodes.label: SubAgentMiddleware — the task tool
nodes.excerpt: Delegation by state subtraction: the subagent's initial state is the parent's minus a curated key set, with messages replaced by the single task description; exactly one ToolMessage returns. Subagents get a smaller stack and no task tool of their own. Fork mode (inherit the history) is opt-in, beta-warned, and refuses recursion at call time.

nodes.label: Backends — BackendProtocol
nodes.excerpt: One protocol decides where files live and whether execution exists: StateBackend (in graph state, cannot execute), StoreBackend, FilesystemBackend (real disk, path-jailed, not isolated), LocalShellBackend (host subprocess, shell=True, under an extended warning), CompositeBackend prefix routing, and the abstract BaseSandbox. The security boundary of the whole system is which backend the application wires in.

nodes.label: Harness + provider profiles
nodes.excerpt: Per-model tuning as data: prompt suffixes, tool-description overrides, extra middleware, exclusions — for built-in Anthropic, OpenAI Codex, and NVIDIA Nemotron families, with public registration functions. The Codex profile is the one place write_todos exists in the package: LangChain's TodoListMiddleware, added for that model's prompting style.

nodes.label: LangChain create_agent() — the loop
nodes.excerpt: Dependency layer (langchain==1.4.5, pinned separately). Compiles a StateGraph: a model node that runs the request through the chained wrap_model_call handlers and invokes the model with tools bound; a tools node; one graph node per middleware state hook; routing edges — no tool calls routes to END, pending calls fan out as one Send each. It adds no middleware of its own, and stamps recursion_limit 9_999 on every graph.

links.label: langchain factory.py:1991-2043 — the model-to-tools routing edge

nodes.label: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware
nodes.excerpt: LangChain's middleware class. Its after_model hook matches the model's pending tool calls against interrupt_on (with when predicates), assembles one review request, and calls LangGraph's interrupt(); decisions are approve / edit / reject / respond. Deep Agents' contribution is generating the interrupt_on config from filesystem permission rules.

links.label: langchain human_in_the_loop.py:481 — interrupt() called with the request

nodes.label: LangChain pieces used as-is
nodes.excerpt: What Deep Agents reuses rather than rebuilds: Anthropic prompt-caching middleware (appended by a Deep Agents helper), LangChain's SummarizationMiddleware composed inside Deep Agents' own as its partitioning and summary engine, and init_chat_model resolving provider:model strings.

links.label: deepagents middleware/summarization.py:627 — the LangChain helper composed

nodes.label: LangGraph Pregel runtime
nodes.excerpt: Dependency layer (langgraph 1.2.15, pinned separately). Bulk-synchronous super-steps: each tick prepares the tasks whose channels updated, runs them concurrently, merges their writes through the channel reducers, and saves a checkpoint (source: loop). The recursion ceiling is checked at the top of tick(); GraphRecursionError is raised only when no stop condition was reached.

links.label: langgraph pregel/_loop.py:786 — checkpoint after every super-step

nodes.label: ToolNode — tool execution
nodes.excerpt: LangGraph's prebuilt tools node, constructed by create_agent with the chained wrap_tool_call wrappers. Executes one tool call per Send task, injects state/store/runtime arguments, returns ToolMessages or Commands — and turns tool exceptions into error ToolMessages by default.

nodes.label: Checkpointer + store
nodes.excerpt: Threads and persistence: a checkpoint when the input lands and after every super-step, and the BaseStore namespaces behind StoreBackend. None of it is configured by default — create_deep_agent passes the caller's checkpointer and store straight through to create_agent, so the default assembly persists nothing across invocations.
